summary: This script creates an interactive Docker logs viewer using fzf (a fuzzy finder). It lists all Docker containers in a searchable menu with a live preview showing container metadata and recent logs, with color-coded output. When you select a container, it either opens the logs for editing or streams them live using the best available tool on your system.

explanations.4: _d_check_env fzf docker || return 1 verifies that both fzf and docker commands exist on the system; if either is missing, the function exits early with return 1.
explanations.9: command -v checks if a program exists in your PATH and sends output to /dev/null to suppress it; the script is checking whether batcat (Debian/Ubuntu's version of bat) is available.
explanations.16: A multi-line string is being built that will be used as the preview window content; the curly braces like {{.Name}} are Go template syntax that docker inspect will replace with actual container values.
explanations.23: The += operator appends a string to the existing preview_cmd variable, building up the full command that will display in fzf's preview panel.
explanations.28: This awk command uses gsub (global substitution) to find ERROR/FATAL/ERR and WARN/WARNING words and wrap them with ANSI color escape codes before printing; red for errors, yellow for warnings.
explanations.34: docker ps -a lists all containers (running and stopped) with tab-separated output; this output is piped into fzf so the user can search and select one.
explanations.35: --ansi tells fzf to interpret ANSI color codes (the escape sequences) in the preview output so colors actually display; without it, you'd see raw escape code gibberish.
explanations.38: --expect=ctrl-e captures the Ctrl-E key press so the script knows whether the user wants to edit the command or just run it.
explanations.43: head -n 1 extracts the first line of fzf_out, which contains the key the user pressed (either ctrl-e or empty if they just hit Enter).
explanations.44: tail -n +2 extracts everything after the first line, which is the container row the user selected (ID, name, status, image).
explanations.45: awk '{print $1}' grabs the first field (whitespace-separated) from the selection, which is the container ID.
explanations.60: print -z places the command string into the zsh line editor buffer so the user can edit it before pressing Enter to execute.
